skill.name: mantis-structural-index
skill.description: Builds a content-addressed semantic-unit index from source code for structural context. Use when a pinned or live codebase is available and structural cross-reference data would improve research quality. Don't use for findings analysis, patching, or reporting.
skill.summary: Guides source indexing with content-addressed caches, symbol queries, and explicit coverage while preserving lexical discovery.
skill.author: google

security_audit.summary: All 225 static matches are documentation syntax or legitimate indexing operations, not the reported threats. Semantic review identifies forgeable helper-version checks and missing remote-query disclosure controls. No evidence found of malicious payloads, credential theft, or audit-directed prompt injection in the supplied skill.

remediation.issue: Executable helper reuse checks a version comment instead of trusted content.
remediation.suggestion: Regenerate helpers from trusted source or verify their complete content against trusted hashes before execution. Reject symlinks and restrict helper-directory ownership and write permissions.

remediation.issue: Remote providers have no explicit endpoint approval or data-disclosure policy.
remediation.suggestion: Default to local queries and require approval for each remote endpoint. Require protected transport, validate destinations, and document which repository metadata may leave the workspace.

content.value_statement: Large source trees make symbol navigation and caller discovery expensive. This skill guides structural indexing with reusable caches and coverage-aware queries while preserving lexical discovery.
actual_capabilities: Guides runtime generation of builder and query helpers for source symbols, call edges, function boundaries, and coverage.
Selects available indexing backends per partition, from matched native indexes to parser, symbol, heuristic, or lexical fallbacks.
Defines content-addressed semantic units for incremental reuse across snapshots.
Specifies bounded symbol resolution, caller and callee lookup, function boundaries, and coverage queries.
Records snapshot provenance, precision, deferred units, and backend metadata in a manifest and SQLite catalog.
Supports advisory integration with planners and researchers while requiring the union with lexical discovery.
limitations: Only an instruction document is supplied; executable helpers are generated at runtime and their behavior depends on the agent.
Index precision depends on installed backends; dynamic dispatch, macros, and indirect calls may be missed.
Large corpora may receive partial coverage, and raw native indexes may require external ingestion.
The skill does not analyze findings, patch code, produce audit verdicts, or determine production build reachability.

use_cases.title: Navigate an Unfamiliar Codebase
use_cases.description: Build source cross-references, resolve ambiguous symbols, and locate enclosing functions before reading implementation details.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Security Research
use_cases.description: Rank candidate call sites with structural hints while retaining every candidate found through repository-wide lexical discovery.

use_cases.title: Reuse Indexing Work Across Snapshots
use_cases.description: Reuse unchanged semantic units and report coverage, provenance, and deferred work for repeated analysis runs.

prompt_templates.title: Index the Current Repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a local structural index for the current repository. Use unknown snapshot provenance, report coverage and backend precision, and preserve source files.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve a Symbol and Its Callers
prompt_templates.prompt: Resolve [symbol name] in [language or file]. Ask me to disambiguate matches, then list paginated caller hints with precision and coverage. Include lexical candidates.

prompt_templates.title: Index a Pinned Snapshot
prompt_templates.prompt: Index [snapshot root] using [snapshot ID] and [state root]. Verify provenance, reuse matching units, keep the snapshot read-only, and report deferred partitions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Large Incremental Build
prompt_templates.prompt: Index [snapshot root] locally with approved backends and verified helpers. Prioritize [target files] and changed units within [unit and byte limits]. Report reuse, remaining work, and coverage without excluding lexical candidates.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: index a live repository using only a heuristic backend.
output: Snapshot provenance: unknown; a fresh build is required.
Backend precision: heuristic; structural matches remain advisory.
Returned artifacts: manifest, SQLite catalog, and query helper.
Coverage summary distinguishes indexed, deferred, and failed files.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: find callers when the relevant partition is only partially indexed.
output: Result status: no indexed callers; coverage is partial.
This does not establish that the function has no callers.
Run lexical discovery and retain all candidates alongside structural hints.

best_practices: Validate snapshot provenance and keep generated artifacts outside pinned source trees.
Verify helper integrity before execution and approve any remote provider before sharing repository metadata.
Inspect precision and coverage, disambiguate symbols, and combine structural results with lexical discovery.
anti_patterns: Treating an empty structural query as proof that no callers exist.
Reusing an unknown-snapshot index against a mutable live tree.
Executing modified helpers solely because their version comment matches.

faq.question: Does this skill include executable indexing scripts?
faq.answer: No. The supplied file defines instructions and contracts. The agent generates builder and query helpers at runtime.

faq.question: Can it run without a pinned snapshot?
faq.answer: Yes. It indexes the current directory with unknown provenance and rebuilds on every invocation.

faq.question: Which indexing backends can it use?
faq.answer: It selects available backends per partition, including matched native indexes, compiler extractors, AST parsers, symbol tools, heuristics, and lexical fallback.

faq.question: Does it replace repository-wide lexical searches?
faq.answer: No. Structural results are advisory. Consumers must retain lexical candidates and combine both result sets.

faq.question: Can it analyze vulnerabilities or generate patches?
faq.answer: No. Its scope is source cross-reference data. Findings analysis, patching, reporting, and production build reachability are outside its scope.

faq.question: Does it send repository information to remote services?
faq.answer: Local indexing does not require a remote provider. Optional remote queries can disclose symbol and file metadata; approve the destination before enabling them.
